outcome_detail: $400,000 settlement by the City of Spokane, reported June 2, 2025.
criminal_detail: Former officer Nathan Nash was convicted by a Spokane jury in September 2022 of second-degree rape with aggravating circumstances in this plaintiff's case (the aggravator being violation of the trust placed in him as a law enforcement officer) and of third-degree rape of a second woman. He was sentenced in October 2022 to 14 years to life in prison and has been appealing.
description: A woman sued the City of Spokane over former police officer Nathan Nash, who raped her in her home in 2019 while following up on a domestic-violence-related call he had responded to on duty. She testified at Nash's criminal trial that he began touching her inappropriately while examining a bruise on her leg, then pushed her onto a couch and raped her; a jury convicted him in September 2022 of second-degree rape with aggravating circumstances for violating the trust she placed in him as an officer, and he was sentenced to 14 years to life. Her suit alleged the city failed to prevent the assaults and to adequately track officer activities. In June 2025, the city agreed to pay her $400,000, following a $300,000 settlement in 2024 with the second woman Nash was convicted of raping (see companion record).
notes: Companion record rec-46 covers the other woman's $300,000 settlement approved in March 2024; the two settlements total $700,000.
